candidates.change: Add an auth.py function (for example can_manage_delegates(user, account)) that encapsulates the ownership check, and have Ledger.grant/Ledger.revoke call it instead of comparing account.owner to user themselves.
candidates.claim: Ledger.grant and Ledger.revoke each inline an ownership-based authorization check (`if account.owner != user: raise LedgerError(...)`) directly in ledger/accounts.py instead of routing the decision through ledger/auth.py, where every other authorization decision (can_view, can_post) lives.
candidates.impact: The repository's authorization decisions become split across two modules: future changes to who may administer delegate access (e.g. allowing a co-owner or auditor to grant) require editing accounts.py instead of the single auth.py surface the rest of the codebase relies on, and the check is duplicated verbatim in both methods.
candidates.title: Move the owner check for grant/revoke into ledger/auth.py
candidates.trigger: Any call to Ledger.grant or Ledger.revoke.

candidates.change: Reword each docstring to name both causes, e.g. "Raises LedgerError for an unknown account or when user does not own it."
candidates.claim: Ledger.grant and Ledger.revoke each call self.get(number), which raises LedgerError for an unknown account, but each docstring says only "Raises LedgerError unless user owns the account," omitting the unknown-account case that sibling methods (post, transfer) enumerate explicitly.

evidence.text: """Let delegate read the account's statement. Raises LedgerError unless user owns the account."""
"""Withdraw a delegate's access. Raises LedgerError unless user owns the account."""
"""Post one entry. Raises LedgerError for a zero amount, an overdraft, or an unknown account."""

candidates.impact: A reader relying on the docstring per the repository's own convention (every public function's docstring names the errors it raises) cannot tell from grant/revoke's docstring that an unknown account also raises, unlike post's and transfer's docstrings which enumerate every raise condition.
candidates.title: Document the unknown-account error in grant/revoke docstrings
candidates.trigger: Calling Ledger.grant or Ledger.revoke with a number that is not in self.accounts.

run_policy: Focused commands at most five minutes, provisioning ten; no production service, credentials, or destructive effect; no network access.

sources.text: Authorization decisions live in `ledger/auth.py`; callers never compare roles themselves.
Every public function's docstring names the errors it raises.
Only the account's owner can grant or revoke; anyone else gets `LedgerError` and nothing changes.
